text:
Maya (Product): Heads-up — ACME (large enterprise pilot) pushed back. They want 100% traffic on day-1 and asked us to exempt their three regions from the canary slice and the 2-hour ramp.
Liam (Eng): Oof. We usually require canaries for safety. Why do they need full traffic immediately?
Alex (AcctExec): ACME legal + ops: they have an internal migration window next month, need cutover. They said staged exposure would break their rollback plan.
Maya (Product): They offered to sign a short-term SLA addendum and extra support hours. Request: "allowlist" the 3 tenants/regions to bypass canary and get priority routing.
Noah (Eng-Platform): We can implement a feature-flag based allowlist per tenant -> route to production pool and skip canary. Technical caveats: bypassing prefix-cache warmup and KV-cache priming increases tail latency risk. Also affects autoscaler signals.
Sara (SRE): If we do this, we need explicit guardrails:
- preflight smoke check (success rate >= 99% for 5m)
- realtime latency p50/p95 and error-rate alerts
- manual kill-switch that re-routes within 30s
Otherwise we can't accept production risk. :warning:
Eva (Solutions): ACME is willing to run shadow traffic for 48hrs ahead of cutover and share their synthetic test harness. That helps. They also want a prioritized support channel for first 24hrs.
Liam (Eng): From implementation side: rough plan — add tenant_allowlist flag in rollout config, and a validation step in the router. Pseudocode:```json
{
  "rollout": {
    "canary_pct": 0.05,
    "allowlist_tenants": ["acme-east","acme-eu","acme-ap"],
    "priority_routing": true
  }
}
```
We need to ensure downstream metrics are tagged so we can filter signal for only allowlist traffic.
Sara (SRE): Also require a pre-cutover runbook section: who hits the kill-switch, who approves, escalation steps to on-call SRE. Add latency SLO targets and rollback criteria. Example rollback triggers: p99 latency > 3x baseline for 10m OR error rate > 1% sustained 5m.
Maya (Product): Proposed launch criteria for exemption: shadow validation >= 95% success for 48h, synthetic passbook from ACME, signed SLA addendum, runbook + two engineers on-call during cutover.
Alex (AcctExec): ACME agrees to the shadow + SLA + support hours. They asked if we can shorten the shadow window to 24h if metrics look excellent.
Noah (Eng-Platform): We can support 24h early-exit if the smoke checks and p95/p99 are within thresholds for 12 continuous hours and no regressions in key metrics. Need explicit automated gating.
Liam (Eng): Implementation tasks (estimates):
- rollout allowlist config + router changes (2d)
- metric tagging and dashboard (1d)
- kill-switch wiring + test (1d)
- runbook + on-call overlap scheduling (0.5d)
Total ~4.5 engineer-days.
Sara (SRE): I'll draft alert thresholds and the kill-switch playbook. Add a pre-cutover canary smoke test script and an automated rollback trigger to the ops pipeline.
Eva (Solutions): I'll collect ACME's synthetic harness and map their tests to our metrics. Also prep priority Slack channel and pager policy.
Maya (Product): Decision? My recommendation: allowlist exemption if ACME accepts our launch criteria + 24h accelerated exit condition. Rollout window: non-business hours for ACME regions, start at 01:00 local, with 2-hour monitoring hold.
Alex (AcctExec): ACME thumbs-up on that plan. They prefer 01:00 but can be flexible.
Liam (Eng): Fine by me. We'll target next-week Wednesday for implementation and schedule a dry-run.
Sara (SRE): I'll be oncall for the dry-run and the actual cutover.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/tenant-allowlist -> staging (build 4821) :rocket:
Maya (Product): Great — action items: @Liam implement config, @Noah add gating, @Sara draft runbook, @Eva coordinate tests with ACME, @Alex get signed SLA. I'll update the rollout doc and ping for final signoff. :eyes:
Liam (Eng): Will open PR and link the staging deploy here.
Noah (Eng-Platform): I'll add gating checks to the pipeline.
Sara (SRE): Adding rollback criteria to the runbook now.
Eva (Solutions): Sync with ACME for shadow traffic start tomorrow 10:00 UTC.
Alex (AcctExec): I'll chase legal for the addendum.
Maya (Product): If anyone sees risk outside these guardrails call it out now. Otherwise we'll follow the plan and reconvene after the dry-run. :thumbsup:
